We need to find the eigenvalues and associated eigenvectors of the matrix ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14068029/assets/b1ba76ba62019524549b4bcf4c36ec2440b2db8f585150a9456218972363a215.png) 

We are given the eigenvalue $\lambda_1 = \textrm{i}$ and the corresponding eigenvector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14068029/assets/f86bdf3e241a51548f8c58fe739e11071197944f5fe2361f83bb34408333211c.png)

**Note:** The eigenvector corresponding to the second eigenvalue $\lambda_2 = \overline{\lambda}_1$ is 
$\mathbf{v}_2 = \overline{\mathbf{v}}_1.$ But we do not require this eigenvector for solving our system.

The solution that we obtain for the eigenvalue $\lambda_1 = \textrm{i}$ and its associated eigenvector is
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14068029/assets/9b2628d7d3c88303bdd7ed2a8aadcdcfe751a01d910f64972a60cc080d039181.png)

We now express this as a real function. Using Euler's formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} \\ 2\end{aligned}]{e}^{\text{i}t} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} \\ 2\end{aligned}]\cdot (\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\text{i}\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ 2\operatorname{cos}⁡t+2\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)+\text{i}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t) \\ 2\operatorname{cos}⁡t+2\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ 2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}]+\text{i}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ 2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}] \\  & ={\text{w}}_{1}(t)+\text{i}{\text{w}}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors $\mathbf w_1$ and $\mathbf w_2$ are linearly independent. Therefore, the general solution of the system is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{x}(t) & ={c}_{1}{\text{w}}_{1}(t)+{c}_{2}{\text{w}}_{2}(t) \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ 2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ 2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, $f(t) = \cos{t} + \sin{t}.$

We are given the eigenvalue $\lambda_1 = 2\textrm{i}$ and the corresponding eigenvector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14068029/assets/9e4e860107360ac18ce72e7f4f07dbf9106de041dea3b6c9228cc30bc45c714e.png)

**Note:** The eigenvector corresponding to the second eigenvalue $\lambda_2 = \overline{\lambda}_1$ is 
$\mathbf{v}_2 = \overline{\mathbf{v}}_1.$ But we do not require this eigenvector for solving our system.

The solution that we obtain for the eigenvalue $\lambda_1 = 2\textrm{i}$ and its associated eigenvector is
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14068029/assets/175d9bde8dda1bfb3a653521add06d23944d72019c0718eed6407abe97f2e87c.png)

We now express this as a real function. Using Euler's formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{2\text{i}t} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} \\ 1\end{aligned}](\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)+\text{i}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t))+\text{i}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}]+\text{i}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}] \\  & ={\text{w}}_{1}(t)+\text{i}{\text{w}}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors $\mathbf w_1$ and $\mathbf w_2$ are linearly independent. Therefore, the general solution of the system is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{x}(t) & ={c}_{1}{\text{w}}_{1}(t)+{c}_{2}{\text{w}}_{2}(t) \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to find the values of $c_1$ and $c_2$ using the initial condition ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14068029/assets/12f33df5f036901c6069ee03a9ba8ccb05cde1071b7add3d1b310da12bb8298d.png) Substituting $t=0$ into the general solution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{x}(0) & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}+{c}_{2} \\ {c}_{1}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the solution to our initial value problem is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{x}(t) & =1[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)-3\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
